candidate_relations.reason: The ECG findings (superiorly directed P waves, long RP interval, short P-wave duration) are characteristic of Atypical AVNRT, not AVRT. While both are reentrant tachycardias involving the AV node, AVRT involves an accessory pathway, which is not indicated here.

While focal atrial tachycardia can present with a narrow complex tachycardia and P waves, the specific ECG findings of superiorly directed P waves (negative in II, III, aVF) and a long RP interval are more indicative of Atypical AVNRT, which is a reentrant mechanism involving the AV node, rather than a focal atrial origin.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Focal atrial tachycardia vs Atypical AVNRT
